sentences.span: markets pricing more to come. But, even though hikes are underway, there are credible reasons why investors risk underestimating the scale of the tightening ahead
sentences.why: Deutsche Bank's own framing is exactly this: the hiking cycle is underway and markets/investors keep underestimating how much further it goes — i.e. the first hike is the start, not the end, of the repricing.

sentences.span: we're back in a globally synchronised rate hiking cycle, with markets pricing more to come
sentences.why: Continuation of s1's DB stance; the sentence pair is one bank's editorial view, directly stated in the source.

No source states the 10-year at exactly 4.99%. Sources place it at 4.95% (17448), 4.925% (17514), 5.00% (17284), 5.02% (17327) and 'around 5%' (17273/17300/17365) on the relevant dates — close but none match 4.99%, and the sentence frames it as a live 'right now' price rather than a research citation.

sentences.span: these agentic workflows require continuous web browsing, API calls, and multi-step execution, they are significantly more CPU- and inference-heavy than basic text queries
sentences.why: GS explicitly ties the consumer-agent (Muse) story to a hardware/compute demand wave; Franklin Templeton (17257) separately states AI infrastructure demand is the 'less uncertain' (i.e. least argued-against) part of the AI trade versus AI outcomes generally.

sentences.span: Apptopia estimated 1.8 million iOS downloads for Muse in the US and Canada, versus 1.3 million for ChatGPT
sentences.why: UBS (17468) cites Apptopia's 1.8m-vs-1.3m US/Canada figure over the equivalent 13-day window, matching the sentence and its (UBS) attribution exactly. Meta +21% vs SPX +1% since launch is separately confirmed in JPMorgan's 17526 ('Meta shares up 21% since the launch of Muse 2 weeks ago, vs. the SPX +1%'), which the sentence does not misattribute since the UBS cite sits only after the download clause.

sentences.span: Samsung HBM4 yields have reportedly reached ~80%, up from below 60% in early mass production ... NAND is also improving, with tech specialists pointing to roughly 20% QoQ pricing upside in both 3Q and 4Q
sentences.why: Goldman (17390) source states both figures verbatim (NAND = flash memory; '3Q and 4Q' = two straight quarters), correctly attributed to Goldman.

sentences.span: Less than 30% of S&P stocks are now above the 50-day moving average
sentences.why: GS Sharkey confirms the sub-30% breadth stat (Goldman-attributed in the sentence). The five-straight-days-more-lows-than-highs-near-a-record clause is separately confirmed verbatim in BTIG's 17474 ('SPX has had five straight days with more 52wk lows than highs even as the index has rallied back near all-time highs'), which the sentence does not misattribute to Goldman.

sentences.span: The CCC minus single-B spread has widened to 799bp, close to the top of its available three-year range
sentences.why: Exact figure match; CCC is the weakest tier and single-B the tier above it.

sentences.span: The six-month ATM implied-volatility spread between IWM and SPX has fallen close to the bottom of its two-year range
sentences.why: Matches 'barely more than' (small spread) and 'near a two-year low' (bottom of two-year range) exactly.

sentences.span: several Republican lawmakers and candidates intensified calls today for the Trump administration to restrict US diesel exports to control retail diesel prices
sentences.why: The $6.29/gallon, +68% from $3.74 figure is an exact match to 17266 (EIA-sourced). But no source shows Trump backing an export ban — only Republican lawmakers pushing the administration to consider one (17527), and GS's 17521 separately calling a curtailment 'unlikely.' The only other trace is a bare CNBC headline-link title ('Trump diesel export ban Ukraine Russia Iran') with no article text confirming a decision. Presenting ongoing political pressure as 'Trump backed an export ban' asserts a decision the sources don't support.

sentences.span: The ICE gasoil crack spread has risen to around $95/bbl this week, up from an average of roughly $74/bbl in August
sentences.why: Exact figure match; the gasoil crack spread is the margin refiners earn turning crude into diesel/gasoil, correctly attributed to ING.

sentences.span: we think this unlikely given it would not solve medium term global supply issues and is expected to get pushback from US refining industry
sentences.why: GS explicitly frames the export curtailment as something the refining industry itself would resist, i.e. a threat to refiners' economics — supporting the sentence's causal claim that the ban is the risk to the refining-margin trade.

sentences.span: This marks the sixth consecutive year the IAEA has revised its projections higher ... where ~60% of new nuclear capacity could come from SMRs, considerably higher than the expected global mix
sentences.why: Both the sixth-consecutive-year detail and the North America SMR-majority detail (~60%, i.e. 'most') match exactly.

sentences.span: the US-South Korea nuclear power investment agreement is set to be signed on September 18
sentences.why: The $96.50/lb record figure actually comes from a different source, Northland (17438: '$96.50/lb, vs. the prior high of $95.00/lb in 2007'); Yuanta's own figure is $97/lb. More importantly, Yuanta's piece (published Sept 14) describes the Sept 18 signing as planned/scheduled ('set to be signed'), not a confirmed completed event — the sentence asserts it as an accomplished fact ('South Korea signed... last Friday'), a conditional/planned event presented as asserted.

sentences.span: uranium prices need to rise to US$120/lb, so as to match supply with demand
sentences.why: Exact match to Yuanta's stated $120/lb level needed to balance supply and demand; the closing invalidation clause is the sentence's own falsifiable framing, not a separate factual claim.
